A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same decayed-identity-shortcut research, despite the broader title and scope in v3. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 reports original MAE representation-learning experiments, ImageNet ablations, reconstruction examples, and supervised ResNet analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds original fine-tuning, COCO segmentation, and diffusion representation-learning and generation results.

M1.justification: The decay formula, MAE encoder-only application, encoder–decoder skip connections, and zero initialization remain unchanged. Section 5 introduces a limited diffusion-specific adaptation: decay extends through the U-ViT decoder, reflecting the different location of useful semantic representations.

E1.justification: v3 adds COCO validation images for semantic grouping and unsupervised segmentation, plus CIFAR-100 diffusion experiments. ImageNet-100 coverage expands to unconditional and class-conditional generation and diffusion representation learning. The original ImageNet classification and appendix supervised experiments remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes MoCo-v2, SimCLR-v2, and iBOT from the reported comparison and adds ConMIM, ADDP with ViT-L, and Latent MIM. Section 5 also introduces unmodified U-ViT, represented by alpha_min = 1.0 in Table 4, as the diffusion comparator.

E3.justification: New evaluation protocols include end-to-end fine-tuning, COCO clustering/postprocessing evaluated with mIoU, and diffusion generation evaluated with FID. Diffusion probing selects the best feature layer and noise level, while ImageNet-100 diffusion uses pretrained-VAE latents. The existing MAE pretraining and linear-probing settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: v3 adds semantic feature-map analysis on COCO, diffusion decay-factor sweeps, generated-image comparisons in Figure 9, and quantitative rank–accuracy correlations in Figure 5c. These substantially extend the analysis of representation structure and decay behavior. Earlier MAE ablations, t-SNE results, reconstruction examples, and supervised rank analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 adds Pearson correlation estimates between feature rank and probing accuracy at seven training epochs in Figure 5c; v2 discusses this association qualitatively. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Matched MAE probing and appendix tables retain their values. Newly reported results include COCO segmentation at 10.41 versus 4.10 mIoU, fine-tuning at 82.9% versus MAE's 83.6%, and class-conditional ImageNet-100 diffusion FID of 4.98 versus 6.93 for standard shortcuts. Section 4.1 also corrects the proposed method's prose score from 72.3% to 72.7%, while retaining a baseline typo of 67.3% instead of Table 1's 67.8%.

T1.justification: Equations 1–6 retain the same residual recurrence, expansion, linear decay schedule, and entropy-based effective-rank definition. No new formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or substantive derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and contributions broaden the central claim from improved MAE feature abstraction to generative representation learning encompassing diffusion models. v3 additionally claims improved diffusion generation quality. The original MAE accuracy and low-rank representation claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the earlier persistent rank–accuracy narrative by acknowledging weaker ordering later in training and proposing compensatory feature-rank growth. It adds arguments about fine-tuning's limitations as a representation-quality measure and potentially suboptimal diffusion decay placement. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit discussion of incompatibility with contrastive objectives.

D1.justification: v3 documents U-ViT model sizes, VAE latent dimensions, default scheduler/sampler references, and COCO clustering choices, although detailed new settings are largely deferred to citations. Appendix A retains MAE hyperparameters, hardware, and training times but removes the explicit L2-loss disclosure for reconstruction visualizations; this does not establish a change to those experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting U-ViT, diffusion representation learning, spectral feature visualization, and newer masked-modeling comparators, while removing the MoCo-v2 and SimCLR-v2 references. iBOT remains cited despite leaving Table 1. The established positioning around residual architectures and low-rank bias is largely retained.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, experiments receive separate MAE and diffusion sections, and embedding analysis becomes a subsection. Selected ablation and discussion paragraphs are rewritten, and citations switch to author–year style. Most existing introduction, method, conclusion, and appendix prose remains.

P2.justification: The opening presentation is redesigned into a results montage and a horizontal architecture diagram. Table 1 replaces its backbone column with separate fine-tuning and probing columns; new semantic visualizations, a diffusion table, and generated-image comparisons are added. The rank figure gains a correlation panel, while retained appendix displays are reformatted and relocated.

improvement.justification: Beyond v2's MAE-focused evidence and supervised appendix analyses, v3 directly tests semantic grouping on COCO and representation learning alongside generation in diffusion models. This substantially strengthens support for the abstraction and applicability arguments. It also quantifies and qualifies the rank interpretation and reports a fine-tuning disadvantage. Incomplete new experimental details, removal of the contrastive-learning caveat, and the remaining text/table inconsistency are drawbacks, but the additional empirical validation provides a clear substantial net gain.
